lede: Latent 8 wins the search. Fashion reconstructs and samples more cleanly than digits, and both are clearer than RealNVP.
title: Digits against Fashion-MNIST
question: With the same VAE, how do reconstruction, likelihood, and prior samples differ on the two datasets?
process: `_vae_loss` in `src/mnist_vae_comparison/model.py` is the per-image sum of squares plus \( \beta \) times the closed-form KL, \( \mathrm{KL} = -\frac{1}{2}\sum_j (1 + \log\sigma_j^2 - \mu_j^2 - \sigma_j^2) \), with \( \beta = 1 \). The decoder is a tanh network and pixels lie in \([-1,1]\). Reconstructions decode the posterior mean. Samples decode 64 draws from \( \mathcal{N}(0,I) \). Optuna compared latent sizes 2, 8, 16, and 32 with hidden size 256, dropout 0.1, learning rate \(10^{-3}\), weight decay \(10^{-6}\), and batch 128. Latent 8 won, validation loss 95.93, against 118.06, 101.37, and 107.42. Both datasets then used that recipe on 1,000 images per class for the scored run. Per-epoch losses were drawn to `loss.png` in each reference cache and were not exported as a series. The panels are the final test scores.

opening.summary: Both priors produce many classes. Fashion garments stay readable and digits stay recognizable, with thin strokes softening first. Those grids are clearer than the RealNVP inverse samples. Fashion’s test ELBO is higher and its domain KID is lower.
opening.hover: Hover a dataset, then the latent-size search.

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Digits test MSE is 0.0852, KL is 15.41, ELBO is −82.21. Domain KID is 3.1052. Prior samples still look like digits, but thin strokes are the first thing a blurry decoder drops, and the spatial KID says those samples sit farther from the test set than the Fashion samples do.
marks.frameCaption: Digits prior samples, N(0, I), latent 8.

marks.summary: Fashion test MSE is 0.0749, KL is 12.34, ELBO is −71.09. Domain KID is 0.2043. Shirts, shoes, trousers, and bags still read as those objects when the decoder is soft, because the silhouette is wide. The same blur hurts a one-pixel stroke much more.
marks.frameCaption: Fashion prior samples, N(0, I), latent 8.

charts.title: Optuna validation loss against latent size

marks.answers: What didn't turn out as expected?
marks.summary: Latent 2 is the worst of the four finished trials, validation loss 118.06. Every other hyperparameter was held fixed: hidden 256, dropout 0.1, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 1e-6, batch 128. The code is too small for the ELBO on this slice.

Latent 8 is bold because it is the minimum validation loss, 95.93, and Optuna minimizes that loss. best_params.json records this trial. The digits and Fashion checkpoints both use it. Latent 16 scores 101.37 and latent 32 scores 107.42, so a wider code made this short search worse.

marks.answers: Why do you think the results might not be great?
marks.summary: Latent 16 scores validation loss 101.37, above latent 8. Four epochs on the slice is a short fit, and the extra coordinates are not yet paying for themselves in the ELBO.

marks.answers: How could the results be improved?
marks.summary: Latent 32 scores 107.42, the second-worst trial. A longer train on the full 60,000 images is the next measurement. The f-VAE run below does use latent 32 on the full split, so it is a different experiment.

reflection.worked: Latent 8 is the best of the four Optuna trials. Both sample grids cover many classes, and they are clearer than the RealNVP inverse grids. Fashion wins the paired scores: test MSE 0.0749 against 0.0852, ELBO −71.09 against −82.21, KL 12.34 against 15.41, domain KID 0.204 against 3.105.
reflection.unexpected: The digit samples look readable and still lose the KID comparison by a wide margin. MSE only moves from 0.085 to 0.075, so pixel error understates the gap the kernel sees. A wider latent made the short search worse, from 95.93 at latent 8 up to 107.42 at latent 32.
reflection.why: A blurry decoder erases a thin stroke and leaves a shirt. These are short slice runs, 4 epochs of search and a scored train on 1,000 images per class. The live reports/mnist_vae_comparison tree is the Fashion cache. The digits numbers live in reference/mnist_digits. Per-epoch curves exist as loss.png and were not written as JSON.
reflection.improve: Retrain both datasets on the full split for more epochs before treating the gap as a property of the data. Export the per-epoch ELBO beside the final panels. The f-VAE digits run uses the full 60,000 images and latent 32, so it is a sharper setup and a separate comparison.
